title: SWAT: Scalable and Efficient Window Attention-based Transformers Acceleration on FPGAs
problem: The quadratic complexity of self-attention computation in traditional Transformers limits long context support, and sliding window-based sparse attention does not align with conventional accelerator microarchitectures, leading to sub-optimal implementations.
motivation: Efficiently supporting long context length is crucial for Transformer models to improve performance and practicality.
method: SWAT is a specialized hardware accelerator built on FPGA (a flexible chip programmable for specific tasks) to run window attention efficiently — where each token only looks at nearby tokens instead of all tokens. It achieves better performance by reusing data across multiple calculations (row-wise dataflow), combining separate processing steps into single operations (kernel fusion), and keeping input data positioned close to where computations happen (input-stationary architecture), all designed around how FPGAs physically organize their memory and computing resources.
key_novelty: The core contribution is matching the hardware's data flow patterns to how window attention naturally accesses data, rather than forcing window attention to fit standard hardware designs.
contributions: FPGA-based accelerator architecture (SWAT) specifically designed for window attention transformers
Row-wise dataflow with kernel fusion optimization for sparse attention computation
Input-stationary design leveraging distributed FPGA memory and computation resources
22× latency and 5.7× energy efficiency improvement over baseline FPGA accelerators
limitations: Scope of applicability to other attention patterns and generalization beyond window attention not discussed.
primary_theme: Dataflow-optimized FPGA acceleration for sparse window attention transformers
